clue.text: Not belonging to a couple agitated about fine

indicators.note: about means going round, so the shuffled letters wrap around the abbreviation for fine
agitated letters are stirred up, so the words to a couple are rearranged

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade and penalty abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A sentence about something that does not suit a quarrelling pair, upset over a penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitated' rearranges TO A COUPLE into OUTOPLACE, and 'about' puts that round F.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something that does not belong where it is sits awkwardly in the wrong spot.

clue.text: Wild gathering sees opera character blowing top

indicators.note: blowing its top means losing its first letter, so the head of the character's name goes

parts.note: Porgy is the title character of Gershwin's opera Porgy and Bess

explanation.surface: A rowdy party where a character from an opera loses his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing top' looks like losing one's temper, but it removes the first letter, P.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a wild, unrestrained party or revel of excess.

clue.text: In expedition across pass following river, I flag

indicators.note: across means stretching over, so the trip's letters straddle the other pieces

parts.note: a tour is a journey or expedition

indicators.note: following puts the mountain pass after the river and the I

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: A climber on an expedition crosses a mountain pass beside a river and plants a flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' means the trip's letters straddle the rest; 'In' at the start is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a three-coloured national banner such as the French one is a kind of flag.

clue.text: Bored, being catered for at college

parts.note: someone catered for is fed
up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A student finds college dull despite having meals provided.
explanation.walkthrough: UP for 'at college' is a British usage: you go up to university and come down when you leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: being tired of something and weary of it is a common informal sense of boredom.

clue.text: On the shelf, Emma may be here?

definitions.text: On the shelf, Emma may be here?

parts.words: On the shelf, Emma may be here?
parts.note: on the shelf suggests a woman left unmarried, but Emma is Jane Austen's novel, which sits on a bookshelf in a book collection

explanation.surface: It seems to ask where a spinster called Emma might be found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the shelf' means unmarried, and Emma sounds like a woman; but Emma is a Jane Austen novel, shelved among books.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: a building or room housing shelves of books is where a novel would stand.

clue.text: Italian wine: Greek character not in favour

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
anti means against, not in favour

explanation.surface: A Greek person turns down an offered Italian wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a red wine from Tuscany is a famous Italian wine.

clue.text: Fish in deep sound

definitions.meaning: the lowest musical register or voice is a low pitch

explanation.surface: A fish swimming in the depths of an inlet.
explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: one sense is a perch-like food fish, the other the lowest musical pitch.

clue.text: Winning answer had to involve ultimate in knowledge

indicators.note: to involve means to take in, so the past form of have encloses a letter
the ultimate in a word is its last letter, here from knowledge

explanation.surface: A quiz contestant is leading thanks to a correct answer drawn from deep knowledge.
explanation.walkthrough: E, the last letter of 'knowledge', goes inside HAD after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a team that is in front or leading is winning.

clue.text: Team devouring chopped livers and some beef

indicators.note: devouring means eating up, so the team's letters swallow the others

parts.note: a side is a sports team

indicators.note: chopped means cut up, so the letters of livers are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sports team eats a meal of chopped liver and a cut of beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopped' rearranges the letters of 'livers'; silverside is a British cut of beef from the hindquarter.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a cut from the outer thigh of a cow, often salted, is a joint of beef.

clue.text: Newcomer having drink outside good public house

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so the drink goes round the other pieces

parts.note: beer is a drink
an inn is a public house

explanation.surface: A newcomer to the pub orders a drink outside a good inn.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone just starting out, a novice, is new to a thing.

clue.text: Monotonous labour of Greek duke around home

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the Greek and duke pair go round the word for home

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: A Greek nobleman's dull household toil.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: dreary, repetitive hard work is called a daily drudge or slog.

clue.text: Newly-wed rightly in prison

parts.note: a bride is a woman just married
well means rightly or properly

explanation.surface: A newly married person deservedly ends up in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridewell was a London prison, and the name became a general word for a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical term: a house of correction or jail, from the London institution of that name.

clue.text: Beef of new policeman drained of energy

indicators.note: new signals a fresh arrangement of the letters left
drained of means emptied of, so a letter is taken out of policeman

parts.note: E is the physics abbreviation for energy

explanation.surface: A grievance raised by a tired new constable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drained of energy' takes E from POLICEMAN, leaving POLICMAN, which 'new' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: to beef means to grumble or gripe, the verb sense.

clue.text: Stop following popular type of music

indicators.note: following puts the word for stop after the word for popular

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
to die is to stop, as an engine dies

explanation.surface: A fan stops listening to a popular genre.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: independent-label alternative rock is a genre of music.

clue.text: Respectable winning position

parts.note: up means ahead, winning, as in two goals up
a standing is a position or rank

explanation.surface: A decent person holding the lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an honest, upright citizen is one of good repute.

clue.text: Issue for year, full of info

indicators.note: full of means containing, so the first pieces enclose the information

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A publication supporting the year's news, packed with information.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: one's offspring or children are one's issue in the legal sense.

clue.text: Fairness: English attribute

parts.note: a quality is an attribute or trait

explanation.surface: A claim that fair play is a typically English trait.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: even-handed treatment with all on the same footing is fairness.

clue.text: Knock tavern sign, unfortunately

parts.note: an inn is a tavern

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters of sign are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone bangs into a pub sign, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batter's knock is their turn at the crease.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket slang: a knock is a batter's turn at the wicket.

clue.text: Kind of timber house, incomplete, in north-eastern music centre

indicators.note: in places the other pieces inside the compass abbreviation

parts.note: ash is a hardwood timber

indicators.note: incomplete means lacking its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a villa is a house

explanation.surface: An unfinished timber house in the north-east, home to music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' drops the final A of the word for house; 'music centre' is the definition, not a hi-fi.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Tennessee city is the capital of country music recording.

clue.text: Finished in the short grass off the fairway

indicators.note: short means missing its last letter, so the is cut back

parts.note: the rough is the long grass beside a golf fairway

explanation.surface: A golfer's round ends with a ball in the long grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: done with or completed, as in we are through.

clue.text: Someone having the potential to succeed

definitions.text: Someone having the potential to succeed

parts.words: Someone having the potential to succeed
parts.note: to succeed reads as doing well, but here means to inherit or follow on in possession of an estate

explanation.surface: A description of a promising young achiever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'succeed' means to inherit, not to do well.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: a woman who stands to inherit a fortune may succeed to it.

clue.text: Training trick daughter studied

parts.note: PE is physical education, training
a ruse is a trick

explanation.surface: A daughter examined a trick in her training.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to read something closely is to have examined it with care.

clue.text: Sales pitch involving large dish

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the sales talk encloses the size letter

parts.note: patter is the glib talk of a salesman
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A salesman's spiel about a big serving plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a large flat serving plate is a kind of dish.

clue.text: Unusual paperback, maybe

definitions.meaning: a paperback may be a work of fiction, a book-length story

explanation.surface: An odd softback book.
explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: fresh and original, and a book-length work of fiction.

clue.text: Privet cut down, surprisingly revealing snake

indicators.note: surprisingly signals an unexpected rearrangement of the letters left
cut down means trimmed, so the last letter of the shrub's name goes

explanation.surface: Trimming a hedge exposes a hidden snake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut down' takes T off PRIVET, and 'surprisingly' rearranges PRIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the adder is a venomous snake of this family.

clue.text: Sluggish, local inhabitant having caught cold on island

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the island letter comes first

parts.note: I is the map abbreviation for island

indicators.note: having caught means holding, so the inhabitant word encloses a letter

parts.note: a native is a local inhabitant
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: An islander lazing about after catching a cold.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes inside NATIVE, with I before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone idle and not moving is lethargic.

clue.text: Out ultimately, a flagstick for undemanding putt?

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter of out is taken

parts.note: the pin is the flagstick on a golf green

explanation.surface: A golfer's ball ends up beside the flagstick, leaving a simple putt.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf term: a very short putt that is easy to knock into the hole.

clue.text: The old man on street's gone by

indicators.note: on means on top of, so in this down entry the father comes above the street

parts.note: pa is father, the old man

explanation.surface: Father has walked past along the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something that has elapsed or is over is in the past.

clue.text: I'm doctor's client, annoyed at waiting time?

parts.note: a patient is someone under a doctor's care

explanation.surface: Someone in the surgery fed up with the wait.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'patient': the person waiting is a patient, but also restless.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: restless and irritated by delay; the question mark flags the playful wording.

clue.text: Starts to photograph old lovers kissing at dance

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Taking a picture of an elderly couple kissing at a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a lively Bohemian couple dance in two-four time.

clue.text: Talk at length about right dress

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the chatter word goes round the letter

parts.note: to gab is to chatter on

explanation.surface: Chattering on about the correct outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: clothing or attire of a particular kind.

clue.text: Severe row within a hospital department

indicators.note: within means inside, so the row sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital
a string is a row or line of things

explanation.surface: A fierce argument inside a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' reads as a quarrel but means a line, STRING.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: harsh or sharply critical, as in a biting comment.
